newLandmarkCandidates.title: Trapped in rebel-held Chang'an, Du Fu writes “Spring View”, then escapes to Fengxiang
Du Fu writes the “Three Officials” and “Three Partings”, then resigns and moves his family to Qinzhou
In Zizhou, Du Fu hears the imperial army has retaken Henan and Hebei and writes his most joyous poem
Having repaid Cao Cao by slaying Yan Liang, Guan Yu seals away Cao's gifts and leaves to rejoin Liu Bei
At Yiyang, Lu Su meets Guan Yu “each bearing only a sword”; Jing is then split along the Xiang River
Zhang Fei captures Jiangzhou and its governor Yan Yan, then frees him, moved by his refusal to yield
About to lead 10,000 troops from Langzhong against Wu, Zhang Fei is murdered by his own officers
Zhou Yu brings troops and grain to Sun Ce at Liyang, helping him cross the Yangtze and take Moling and Qu'e
Zhou Yu and Sun Ce capture Wancheng; Sun Ce weds the elder Qiao sister and Zhou Yu the younger
Hiding in Xiapi, Zhang Liang fetches an old man's shoe on a bridge and receives a book of strategy
Seeing Liu Bang into Hanzhong, Zhang Liang urges him to burn the plank roads to reassure Xiang Yu
Sima Qian defends the defeated general Li Ling, suffers castration, and resolves to finish his history
Exiled to Chaozhou, Han Yu writes “Address to the Crocodiles”; locals name the Han River after him
As prefect of Kuizhou, Liu Yuxi turns Ba folk tunes into his “Bamboo Branch Songs”
Li Qingzhao marries Zhao Mingcheng in Kaifeng; the couple pawn clothes to buy rubbings and antiquities
Ningyuan–Jinzhou victory: Yuan Chonghuan and Zhao Shuaijiao repel Hong Taiji's assault
Newly a jinshi at nineteen, Kou Zhun governs Badong and writes “a lone boat drifts all day long”
Palace general Su Wu sets out from Chang'an bearing the Han tally as envoy to the Xiongnu
After nineteen years in captivity, a white-haired Su Wu returns to Chang'an, his envoy's tally bare
Wei Zheng joins the Wagang rebel leader Li Mi at Luokou as his secretary
After the Xuanwu Gate coup, Wei Zheng answers Li Shimin's rebuke with candor and is promoted
Wei Zheng dies; Emperor Taizong mourns that he has lost the “mirror” that showed his faults
As judge of the Court of Revision, Di Renjie clears 17,000 backlogged cases in a year without complaint
Framed by Lai Junchen, Di Renjie smuggles out a plea on silk, escapes death and is demoted to Pengze
Prefect Di Renjie calms Weizhou as the Khitans retreat; grateful locals build him a living shrine
Di Renjie dies in Luoyang after recommending Zhang Jianzhi; Empress Wu weeps that “the court is empty”
Magistrate Bao Zheng of Tianchang cleverly unmasks a culprit who cut out a farmer's ox tongue
Governing Duanzhou, home of famed inkstones, Bao Zheng leaves office without taking a single one
When Qin expels foreign advisers, Li Si's memorial persuades the King to revoke the order
Framed by Zhao Gao, Li Si is executed in Xianyang, longing to hunt hares with his son once more
Xu Xiake explores Mount Tiantai and opens his travel diaries; that May 19 is now China Tourism Day
On his second Huangshan trip, Xu Xiake scales Tiandu and Lotus peaks and records the climb
Xu Xiake's great southwest journey reaches Tengyue, where he documents volcanic rock and hot springs
Crippled by illness, Xu Xiake dies at home in Jiangyin, leaving over 600,000 characters of travel notes
As prefect of Kaifeng, Bao Zheng opens the gates to direct petitions and becomes a byword for integrity
